page.layout: One printed page. At the head, the running title "PARS SECVNDA." with page number 87 at the right. Below it, two engraved medallion portraits side by side. Under them, one column of running text. At the foot, the signature "Fff 4", set right of centre. No marginal notes.

main_text.p: FL. CL. IVLIANVS natus Constantinopoli, patre Constantio, Constatini Magni fratre, matre Basilina, forma liberali fuit, ingenio callido, ad literas & ad arma apto. Huc Constantius patruelis, Magni filius Constantini, adoptauit, Cæsarē fecit, ad Gallias tuedas misit. hostes hinc profligat, Gallias Alemannorum incursu vastatas, sub primum accessum, præter omnium spem asserit, regemq; Germanorum capit. Agrippinam (quę nunc Colonia dicitur) recipit. Deinde assensu totius exercitus Parisiis Imperator & Augustus vocatur an. mun. 4325. à Christo nato 3 6 3. Ad Constantium literas mittit exorans vt qui licet repugnans, Imperator fit à militibus appellatus, in cōsortiū Imperij admittatur: renuit Constatius. Ad bellum ciuile parat se Iulianus, item & Constatius, qui nihilominus febre correptus, cum deficeret successore statuit Iulianum. Adepto itaq; Imperio solus rerum summa potitus Iulianus, Persis bellū mouet: verùm à transfuga quodā Persa in insidias deductus, cùm eum hinc inde Parthi vrgeret, ab vno ex hostibus, & quidē fugiente, conto percutitur: & cū Philosophis de immortalitate animæ tractās, paulò post moritur, anno ætatis 31. Imperij, mensibus 19. à morte Constantini patruelis. Hic aduersus fidem Christianam libros edidit. Egna. lib. 1. Pomp. Læ. Aure. Vict.

IVVIANVS, seu Iouianus, è Pannonia, mortuo Iuliano electus est princeps, & statim Antesignani Iuuianum clamauerunt: tunc qui in medio, quíque postremi erant milites, opinati Iulianum reuixisse, ingenti lætitia effusi, choreas ducebāt. Hic cum Parsis fœdus icit, Trāstigritanas provincias quinq; reddidit: atq; Arsaci Armeniæ regi, Ro. socio, & amico, opē ferre vetitus est. At è Persīde rediēs hyeme aspera, ingressus cubiculum noui tectorij, positis etiam ibi prunis, ex cruditate insuper stomachi periit, anno ætatis 33. Imperij mensibus 7. Vide vt supia,

page.notes: Two engraved medallion portraits above the text, not transcribed as text. Left medallion: a bearded man in profile, helmeted, with a legend reading "IVLIANVS P F AVG" (the legend is partly worn, with "D N" at the lower left). Right medallion: a younger man in profile, with a legend reading "IOVINIANVS P F AVG" (with "D N" at the lower left). Legends are set around the medallion rims and read clockwise. The line "3 6 3." is printed with spaces between the digits, copied as printed. The final word "supia," is printed with a comma and is copied as printed; it may be a printing error for "supra," but this is left as printed.
